turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hi there, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Quamer Sant, one of the dermatologists here. Did you find parking okay? That garage is a maze.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ah, it really is. I went around twice before I found a spot on level 3.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Everybody does.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So before we start,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: can you tell me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ashling Brennan, and my birthday is June 9th, 1988. Thank you, Ashling.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Your referral mentions a mole on your back.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Tell me what's going on with it. So it's on my left upper back, kind of by my shoulder blade. My husband Declan noticed it looked different back in um,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: July.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: He says it's gotten bigger and darker since spring. Okay, has it bled at all, or crusted over? No, no bleeding.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it itch or hurt?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It itches a little now and then, it doesn't hurt.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you ever had a skin cancer yourself, or any moles removed?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I've never had skin cancer, and nothing's ever been removed.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anyone in the family with skin cancer?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My dad had a basal cell on his nose a few years ago. They scraped it off and he's been fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good to know. How about sun exposure? Sun burns growing up, tanning beds.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, lots of sun. I was a lifeguard every summer through college at Crestview Aquatics. I got burned pretty badly a few times, like blistering. Never did tanning beds, though. Got it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any medicines you take regularly?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Just Levothyroxine. 75 micrograms every morning for my thyroid.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And any allergies to medications? Or to lidocaine or latex?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No allergies that I know of.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Alright, let me take a look. Can you slip your left arm out of the gown?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So on your left upper back, just over the shoulder blade, there's a 7mm dark brown mold. It's asymmetric, the border is irregular and kind of gnarched at the bottom, and there's a black area on one side. Under the dermatasco, I see an irregular network, and a few darts at the edge. That one stands out from your other moles.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is that bad?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It's what we call an ugly duckling. It doesn't look like its neighbors. Let me check the rest of you first. Your back, chest and arms have scattered two to three millimeter round moles, evenly brown. Those all look like normal benign moles. scalp face and legs look fine I don't feel any swollen lymph nodes in your left armpit or your neck any lumps you've noticed in your armpit no nothing like that okay so here's what I think this mole on your back has several changing features most of these turn out to be an atypical mole but I can't rule out an early melanoma just by looking so I'd like to do a biopsy today today okay what does that involve it's a shave biopsy I numbed the area with a little lidocaine with epinephrine then I take off the whole mole with a thin blade fairly deep and send it to the lab no stitches you'll have a shallow wound kind of like a scrape that's fine let's do it great a little pinch and a burn now okay and that's done it went well I've sent it to pathology for care keep the bandage on for 24 hours, then wash it gently once a day, put on plain petroleum jelly and a fresh bandage every day until it heals. That's usually one to two weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, when will I know?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Results take about seven to ten days. They'll post to the portal and someone will call you either way. What's the best number for you? My cell 555 -0163 and my portal email is Aisling Dart Brennan 88 at fastmail .com Got it. If it does come back as a melanoma, we talk about a wider excision to get clear margins, but let's not get ahead of ourselves. If the sight gets red, hard, swollen or drains pus, call us.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, should I be doing anything about the sun? Yes,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: broad spectrum sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher, every day on exposed skin, reapply every two hours when you're outside and a wide brimmed hat. Check your own moles once a month and since you've had blistering sunburns and quite a few moles I'd like to see you for a full skin check every year.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's book a follow -up for the biopsy site and results on Tuesday October 27th. Any other questions?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No I think that's it. Thank you. You're welcome Ashley.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Take care and good luck getting out of that garage.
